summary: Round 2 verification: all five round-1 surviving mutations are CONFIRMED DEAD, each re-measured in a review tree at the staged bytes (baseline :format:test/:sequencer:test/:ingest:test green). (1) pointerEpoch=0;pointerSequence=0 -> 2 failures; pointerEpoch=0 alone -> 1; the original log.nextSequence() off-by-one -> 2. (2) pre-ADR `existing.lastAppliedFlushSeq() > incoming...` across incarnations -> aRestartedPodsSecondCommit... FAILED; and the opposite over-correction `(existing,incoming)->incoming` -> aPodsFlushSeqNeverGoesBACKWARDS... FAILED, so both directions are pinned. (3) `version > VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` -> anUNKNOWNVersionSTOPS... FAILED. (4) deleting the three PodState guards -> 3 distinct failures, one per guard; deleting the null-slot requireNonNull -> aNullSlotIsRefused FAILED. (5) deleting CommitRequest's incarnation guard -> aBlankOrNullIncarnationIsRefused FAILED; reverting FakeSequencer to the two-arg SegmentCommit -> theFakeCopiesTheRequestsTriple... FAILED. Also re-measured and dead: hoisting the delta attribution to segments.get(0) (GoldenAttributedTest + AttributedDeltaTest), swapping epoch/sequence in the v1 pod decode (4 failures), forcing the v1 presence flag true (golden), and minting the incarnation per flush in DefaultIngest (theIncarnationIsMintedOncePerIngestInstance...). RED RECORDS ARE HONEST: every new test in .harness/tdd/red.log failed with AssertionFailedError/AssertionError, never a compile error -- PodStateInvariantTest at lines 34/42/53/65/79, CheckpointWriterContentTest at 91 and 117, CommitRequestTest at 41, FakeSequencerTest at 53. The CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest edit is a STRENGTHENING, not a weakening: I restored the removed `known[7]=VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` assertion alongside the range mutation and it passed, so it killed nothing the new negative-version case does not. One major remains, found by mutation and not previously raised.

findings.title: The v1 pod-slot decode has FOUR new untrusted reads and NOT ONE refusal case; the file whose contract is that every decode bound is undeletable contains no VERSION_ATTRIBUTED fixture at all.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. Checkpoint.java:322-330 adds four reads on the untrusted-decode path under VERSION_ATTRIBUTED -- the presence flag, incLen, epoch, sequence -- plus one new bounds guard. `grep -n 'VERSION_ATTRIBUTED|attributed' CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest.java CheckpointPodStateTest.java` returns only comments: every refusal fixture in the file is built from CheckpointTest.fixture() or oneStream(), both of which encode PodState.bare, i.e. the v0 layout. Two mutations survive the entire suite. MUTATION A -- delete the whole incLen guard at Checkpoint.java:323-327 (`if (incLen < 0 || incLen > c.remaining()) throw ...`), leaving `long incLen = c.uvarint(); String inc = new String(c.bytes((int) incLen), UTF_8);`: `:format:test` and `:sequencer:test` are BUILD SUCCESSFUL. I then proved it is ACCEPT-WITH-WRONG-DATA, not merely uncaught, with a throwaway probe: encode `new Checkpoint(1, Map.of(), Map.of("poda", new PodState("inc", 5, 2, 3)))` (24 bytes, incLen at index 18) and splice that one byte with the uvarint of 0x1_0000_0003 = {0x83,0x80,0x80,0x80,0x10}. Unmutated: `IOException: a checkpoint claims a 4294967299-byte incarnationId but only 5 bytes remain`. Mutated: ACCEPTED, printing `{poda=PodState[incarnationId=inc, lastAppliedFlushSeq=5, epoch=2, sequence=3]}`. That is byte-for-byte the defect this same file already documents as measured for its siblings -- 'a podId length narrows to 1 and eats a byte of the next field', 'a partitionId of this value decodes to partition 1' -- reintroduced for incarnationId, the field ADR-0036 exists to carry, with no test. MUTATION B -- widen the presence-flag condition at Checkpoint.java:322 to `version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.remaining() > 0 && c.uvarint() == 1`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL again. That turns a v1 checkpoint truncated in its last pod slot from REFUSED into ACCEPTED as a bare slot -- a pod whose idempotency pointer silently vanishes from an object read out of the store, which is the unbounded-detection case the row says the pointer exists to prevent. This is the same severity class as tr-3 and tr-4, which the author fixed this round: a guard on bytes from an object store, deletable with the suite green. The remedy is roughly fifteen lines in one existing file -- a v1 fixture spliced with WIDE_NEGATIVE/WIDE_ONE at incLen, and a v1 object truncated after a pod's watermark -- not a split.
findings.surviving_mutation: Checkpoint.java:323-327 -- delete the incLen bounds guard entirely; and independently Checkpoint.java:322 -- `version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.uvarint() == 1` becomes `version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.remaining() > 0 && c.uvarint() == 1`. Each leaves :format:test and :sequencer:test BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

findings.title: Giving every pod and zombie its own incarnation constrains nothing today: `Issued` drops incarnationId, so no assertion can observe it, and no pod ever reissues a flushSeq under a new incarnation.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: I reverted both `incarnations.computeIfAbsent(...)` call sites (lines 227 and 243) to the previous literal "i1" and ran `:sequencer:test --rerun-tasks`. BUILD SUCCESSFUL, with TEST-binjava.sequencer.CommitProtocolSimulationTest.xml and TEST-binjava.sequencer.CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.xml both present in sequencer/build/test-results/test, so the simulation genuinely ran. The reason is structural: `Issued` is `(podId, flushSeq, segmentKey)` and never captures incarnationId, so both CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest sweeps key on `i.podId() + "#" + i.flushSeq()` -- the very pair ADR-0036 rejects -- and cannot tell a diversified fleet from a shared one. Worse for the forward-looking argument in the added comment: `nextFlushSeq` is keyed on the BARE podId (lines 155, 229, 245) and is never reset, so when a pod's incarnation changes across the l:/z: split its flushSeq keeps ascending rather than restarting at 0. The one scenario ADR-0036 exists for -- a new incarnation reissuing flushSeq 0 -- therefore still appears in no seed, and a future M4.10d dedup keyed on the pair would remain indistinguishable from one keyed on the triple in every seed. DETERMINISM IS NOT BROKEN, and I confirmed it rather than assuming: the incarnation values are pure functions of the map key and the seed, `computeIfAbsent` never draws from `random`, nothing iterates the map, and CommitProtocolSimulationTest's two-run replay of seed 99 passes in the unmutated baseline. So the change is inert rather than harmful. It lands as a minor -- the fix is to add incarnationId to `Issued` and reset `nextFlushSeq` when a pod's incarnation changes, which is M4.10d's fixture work, not this row's.
findings.surviving_mutation: CommitProtocolSimulation.java:227 and :243 -- replace both `incarnations.computeIfAbsent(...)` expressions with the literal "i1". :sequencer:test stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
